item.title: How is the PLA countering small FPV drones and their swarms?
item.description: Small multirotor and first-person view drones are now widely used – and one of the most challenging new threats – on the modern battlefield. These drones are small, they fly at low altitudes usually off the traditional air defence radars, and combined with their manoeuvrability they are difficult to detect. A camera on an FPV drone gives the operator a live video feed that can be viewed through goggles, a headset or screen. These drones can be used for precision strikes against personnel,...

item.title: Washington’s ‘missteps’ narrow US lead over China in annual Asia power ranking
item.description: China has narrowed its power gap with the US in Asia to a record low, largely due to Washington’s own “missteps”, according to an Australian think tank’s annual gauge. The 2026 edition of the Lowy Institute’s Asia Power Index, released on Sunday, painted a picture of an “increasingly contested regional balance of power”. item.title: Welfare chief pledges long-term social worker support for Tai Po fire victims
item.description: Hong Kong’s welfare chief has pledged to maintain social worker support for victims of the Wang Fuk Court fire, saying mental health and trauma care for the bereaved and seriously injured will last “years, even decades”. item.title: China’s Sanxingdui silk discovery suggests ancient writing may have existed on perishable cloth
item.description: In the world of archaeology, especially when it comes to ancient societies, organic materials can often lead to breakthroughs, making them particularly valuable artefacts. In Sanxingdui, home to the ancient Shu people (c. 1046–316 BC), the recent discovery of silk residues adhering to 101 artefacts – including bronze, ivory, jade and gold – suggests that silk had already become a valuable commodity. item.title: Despite Serbia’s political earthquake, China hopes ties will stay rock solid
item.description: Beijing has signalled its readiness to maintain close ties with Serbia’s new government, as the victorious Student List prepares to take power and scrutinise major public projects, including those involving Chinese firms.
